name: Palestinian nationalism
summary: Palestinian nationalism is the national movement of the Palestinian Arabs for self-determination and sovereignty in Palestine, born in opposition to Zionism and the loss of 1948. Its mainstream, the secular PLO and Fatah, holds that Palestinians form one nation with a right of return, that Israeli occupation is illegitimate, and that Palestinians are owed a state with Jerusalem as capital, which after 1988 and 1993 it sought on the 1967 territories alongside Israel. It has little shared economic or social program, and an Islamist wing led by Hamas disagrees on religion, borders and means.
scope: The mainstream secular PLO/Fatah strand as expressed in the 1968 Palestinian National Covenant (for the founding armed-struggle and one-state claims), the 1988 Declaration of Independence and the 1993 PLO letters of recognition (for the later two-state, democratic and anti-terrorism commitments). Where these differ the 1988-1993 position is treated as the committed adherent's present view. Hamas and Islamist nationalism, and leftist factions such as the PFLP, are excluded and noted as dissenting strands.

keyFigures.name: Yasser Arafat
keyFigures.role: Long-time PLO chairman and Fatah leader who proclaimed the 1988 declaration and signed the 1993 recognition letters.

keyFigures.name: Amin al-Husseini
keyFigures.role: Grand Mufti of Jerusalem and leader of the early Palestinian national movement.

keyFigures.name: Mahmoud Abbas
keyFigures.role: Fatah leader and Palestinian Authority president who advocates statehood on the 1967 lines.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Nationalists list a right to health care among demanded rights, though the movement has no worked-out health program; inferred from that and from PLO-era social services.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Labor rights feature in the nationalist platform but wage policy is not a defining issue, so this is inferred from the labor-rights emphasis.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Mainstream nationalism has no stated economic doctrine; Fatah has mixed state-led and market elements, so adherents are split.

public-ownership.rationale: Economic ownership was never central; the movement subordinated economic questions to national liberation.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No documented stance; economic policy varies across Fatah, PLO left factions and the PA.

unions-good.rationale: Labor rights and workers' organization are among the freedoms nationalists demand, but unions are not a doctrinal pillar.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property is salient mainly as restitution of refugee property, which pulls toward property rights, while no general doctrine exists.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Not addressed; no distinctive doctrine of corporate regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Nationalists stress social rights for a dispossessed, refugee-heavy population, so cutting welfare is inferred as disfavoured.

worker-ownership.rationale: Left PLO factions might favor it but the mainstream is silent; adherents are split.

surveillance-ok.rationale: A movement long subject to occupation security surveillance, whose declaration commits to civil liberties, would lean against, though PA security practice differs.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; conservative Palestinian social norms make legalization unlikely to be endorsed.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The declaration commits to free expression and nondiscrimination; the movement has no stated view on hate-speech law.

strong-leader.rationale: Nationalism has been centered on strong figures like Arafat, yet the declaration promises parliamentary democracy; split.

state-harmful.rationale: The movement's central goal is to build a sovereign state with institutions, constitution and judiciary, as in the 1988 declaration.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; armed resistance is part of the tradition but domestic gun law is not a nationalist issue.

empower-police-military.rationale: A movement seeking statehood wants security forces of its own, yet it also criticizes militarized occupation; split.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the predominantly conservative Muslim and Christian social norms of the society.

decide-locally.rationale: The Covenant treats Palestine as a single indivisible unit and national unity as a motto, implying priority for national over local authority.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed by any source; no distinctive penal doctrine.

traditional-family.rationale: Inferred from the largely conservative social outlook of the society; secular factions are less committed, so low confidence.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not a nationalist platform issue; inferred from prevailing Palestinian social attitudes and the absence of any such demand.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from prevailing social norms in Palestinian society.

more-religion-public.rationale: Secular PLO factions long dominated while Islamist movements want more; the movement is split.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Nationalists demand redress for the historical injustice of 1948 dispersal, but 'racial' injustices in the usual sense are not their theme.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split between secular and religious outlooks.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Covenant treats Palestinian identity as a permanent inherited trait that must be preserved and developed despite dispersal.

gradual-change.rationale: The movement is a liberation struggle seeking to overturn an existing order, though it accepted negotiated stages after Oslo.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Palestinians are refugees and diaspora not a receiving society; immigration restriction is not a nationalist topic, though Israeli immigration is opposed as settlement.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The movement relies on UN resolutions for legitimacy and its declaration pledges adherence to the UN Charter, so it favors a stronger UN role.

free-trade.rationale: No stated doctrine; Palestinian economic nationalism and PA trade arrangements pull in different directions.

nation-first.rationale: The movement prioritizes its own national claim yet commits to UN principles and the Non-Aligned Movement; split.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Palestinians want international protection from occupation but are wary of Western force, and the sources do not address it.

open-borders.rationale: The movement seeks sovereign borders and control of them while demanding freedom of travel for Palestinians; inferred lean against.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; development under occupation is a priority, so growth limits are unlikely to appeal.

revolution-justified.rationale: The Covenant calls armed struggle the only way to liberate Palestine and the Declaration affirms resistance to occupation; the movement is a national liberation movement.

experts-over-public.rationale: The declaration envisions a parliamentary democracy with popular sovereignty, implying no special expert authority.

central-planning.rationale: No endorsement in nationalist sources; the mainstream is not committed to planned economies, though some leftist factions were.

socialized-markets.rationale: No stated doctrine; economics subordinate to national liberation.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Early nationalist societies promoted national industries, but no modern tariff doctrine exists; inferred lean is weak.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Early societies promoted national industries; the modern PA has no clear doctrine; split.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Not addressed; land attachment is central but economic structure is not.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Not addressed; nationalist mainstream is not communist, so inferred rejection.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; a state-building movement wants its own monetary institutions, inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: The declaration promises parliamentary democracy with the right to form parties, though Fatah dominance in practice blurs this.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The declaration envisions a constitutional parliamentary democracy, and the nationalist tradition is republican.

democracy-best.rationale: The 1988 declaration commits to a parliamentary democratic system with free parties and an independent judiciary, though Islamist strands differ.

direct-votes.rationale: The declaration sets a parliamentary system; referenda are not discussed.

workers-councils.rationale: The declaration sets parliamentary institutions; councils are a leftist-faction idea not in the mainstream.

right-to-secede.rationale: The movement treats Palestine as indivisible, yet claims self-determination for itself; no stance on secession generally.

natural-rulers.rationale: The declaration's equality of rights and democratic order reject innate rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Covenant calls armed struggle the only path and permanent strategy; even later moderation kept a right of resistance.

war-builds-character.rationale: Armed struggle is valued as a means to liberation, not for building character; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: Secular PLO factions favor separation while Islamist strands reject it, so the movement is genuinely split.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Mainstream secular nationalism opposes scriptural law, though Islamist nationalists such as Hamas favor it.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The declaration calls for state institutions and an independent judiciary; state security is a core aim.

military-superiority.rationale: Palestinians lack a state army and the declaration pledges peaceful settlement; inferred disfavour.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Covenant defines the nation as Arab Palestinians, but the 1988 declaration promises equality regardless of religion, race or sex; split.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The mainstream places national liberation above class; only leftist factions like the PFLP emphasize class.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Palestinians claim themselves as the native people with sovereignty over their homeland, rejecting other claims.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not explicit in core sources, but anti-colonial framing implies support; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: The Covenant ties Palestine to Arab unity and the Declaration calls the state part of the Arab nation, though mainstream puts Palestine first.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Not addressed; collective national duty is emphasized.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The Covenant stresses duty to liberate the homeland, while the declaration affirms individual rights; split.

limit-population.rationale: Demography is a central national concern; Palestinians reject limits and dispute demographic framing of return.

restore-past-order.rationale: Return and restitution of 1948 losses is central, yet the movement is forward-looking about statehood; split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The shift from the Covenant to Oslo shows pragmatism, but liberation principles are held firmly; split.

direct-action.rationale: Fatah combined guerrilla action, the intifada and electoral politics; mainstream does not choose one over the other.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Nowhere advocated; the movement seeks a modern state.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not addressed; inferred rejection by a non-communist mainstream.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Not addressed; leftist factions might agree, mainstream silent.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Not addressed; only leftist factions would endorse.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Inferred: the declaration's parliamentary democracy excludes class dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Not addressed; attachment to land by individual families is common.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The Covenant links Zionism to imperialism, but no general theory of capitalism and war is stated.

taxation-theft.rationale: A state-building movement relies on a state and its institutions.

harm-principle.rationale: The declaration promises liberties but nothing on the limit of state restriction.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Collective national rights are central to the Covenant and Declaration, though individual rights are affirmed too.

conscription.rationale: Covenant calls on all Palestinians to join the struggle and form a popular army, but conscription itself is not stated.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Palestinians claim a right to return and stay in the homeland; exile is the problem, not the remedy.

state-as-business.rationale: The declaration envisions a state with rights-bearing citizens, not customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Nationalists demand rights to health care and travel as well as freedoms, implying material conditions matter.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The declaration commits to nonracial equality and the movement frames itself in national, not racial, terms.

organic-representation.rationale: The declaration calls for parliamentary democracy with parties.

total-state.rationale: The declaration promises free expression, parties and an independent judiciary.

national-rebirth.rationale: Early nationalist societies and the movement stress revival of the nation after the Nakba, but decadence rhetoric is not core.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The state is declared within Palestinian territory; the movement opposes expansion, claiming only its own homeland.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Parliamentary democracy under a constitution rules this out.

bound-labor.rationale: The declaration guarantees equality of rights; no source supports bound labor.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not addressed by core sources, though Palestinian scholars contest dominant narratives.

universal-morality.rationale: The declaration appeals to universal human rights and UN principles.

single-common-good.rationale: Not addressed; the declaration endorses pluralist parties.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The Covenant denies Jewish statehood claims and the PLO's 1988 and 1993 positions, while recognizing Israel's existence, still reject Israel as the realization of a Jewish right in Palestine.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The Declaration and Covenant assert Palestinians' right of return wherever they may be; the PA calls it non-negotiable.

revive-national-language.rationale: Arabic remains in everyday use, so the question has little relevance; no stated stance.

rule-by-example.rationale: The declaration builds legitimacy on constitution and law.

national-self-determination.rationale: Self-determination in their own state is the movement's central claim, in both Covenant and Declaration.

force-without-un.rationale: The movement relies on UN legitimacy, but also recognizes a right to self-defense; split.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The movement demands services for refugees in host states, but state welfare design is not addressed.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; high unemployment under occupation makes work tests unlikely to appeal.

class-collaboration.rationale: The mainstream puts national unity above class conflict, per the 'national unity' motto.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The Covenant treats preservation of Palestinian identity and heritage as a duty.

dominated-front.rationale: The Covenant and Declaration place Palestine within the Arab nation and Non-Aligned Movement and describe Zionism as tied to imperialism.

workers-nation.rationale: The mainstream puts national liberation above class loyalties.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The declaration promises equal rights regardless of sex.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed; Islamist strands may favor it, secular ones not.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The declaration prohibits discrimination by race, religion, colour or sex.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Only leftist factions use class analysis of the state.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed for Palestinians; Israeli settlement is opposed rather than assimilation addressed.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not a nationalist theme; the declaration commits to equality and the Palestinian grievance concerns displacement by Zionist settlement, not elite conspiracy.

proportional-representation.rationale: Parliamentary democracy was promised; the PA adopted proportional lists in 2006 under Palestinian law, inferred.

national-mission.rationale: The movement claims its own state, not a mission to spread its government, and pledges non-alignment.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The declaration promises sex equality; adherents split on structural analysis.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Criticism of the PA and factional leaders is widespread among Palestinians, though not a doctrine of the movement.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: The declaration guarantees equal rights without discrimination.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from nationalists' demand for accountability for abuses by Israeli forces and the movement's rights language.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The declaration envisages a state with broad responsibilities and rights guarantees.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The declaration promises complete equality of rights regardless of race, religion, colour or sex.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The Covenant describes Zionism as tied to imperialism and Israel as its instrument, and nationalists treat Zionist settlement as dispossessing Palestinians.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The declaration promises equality regardless of religion but personal status law is divided among confessions; split.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The declaration's pledge of religious equality implies freedom of belief.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not a Palestinian concern; inferred rejection given the majority-Muslim society.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Not addressed; secular and Islamist strands differ.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The declaration grounds the state in the will of the people and parliamentary democracy.

population-transfer.rationale: Palestinians treat the 1948 expulsion as the founding injustice and demand return, so they oppose forced transfer of a minority.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The PLO renounced terrorism in 1993 and rejects force against other states in the Declaration, but keeps a right of resistance to occupation.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The declaration stresses peaceful coexistence and UN principles over struggle as progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed; the movement itself has been banned elsewhere and promises party freedom.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Resistance to foreign domination is the core, but the republican concept is not stated.

separated-powers.rationale: The Declaration promises an independent judiciary and parliament under a constitution.

vanguard-party.rationale: Only the leftist factions like the PFLP take a vanguard view.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Inferred from refugee-focused social rights, not a stated doctrine.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labor rights are claimed, so restrictions are unlikely favoured.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Palestinians attribute their poverty to dispossession and occupation, not population growth.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The declaration celebrates the land of three faiths and promises minority rights.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The declaration envisions a parliamentary system with elections.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The declaration promises rights and judicial independence, yet PA emergency practice varies.

party-controls-media.rationale: The declaration promises freedom of expression.

party-commands-army.rationale: A parliamentary democracy would place forces under the state, though factional armed wings blur this.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Not addressed by any source; Palestinians are demanding citizenship rights, not setting waiting periods.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The Covenant treats Arab unity as a goal, but pooling sovereignty in supranational bodies is not discussed.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Not addressed; the PA presidency holds strong powers in practice but doctrine is silent.

clerical-rule.rationale: Secular PLO factions dominated the movement and the declaration calls for parliamentary democracy, though Islamists dissent.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not addressed; PA presidency practice is contested.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The movement commits to non-alignment but has no army or foreign bases question.

people-in-arms.rationale: The Covenant calls for a popular liberation war with armed fighters as the nucleus of a popular army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not addressed, though attachment to village land is a strong national theme.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The declaration and PLO treat Palestinians in West Bank, Gaza and diaspora as one nation seeking one state.

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed; PA law retains it while many nationalists object.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from social conservatism of society.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed by any source; no nationalist position on curriculum science.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from social norms.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The Covenant defines Palestinians by descent, through the father, a status that persists despite dispersal.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The declaration promises minority rights but no exemptions are discussed.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Non-Aligned commitment and anti-imperialist stance suggest sympathy; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Covenant links Zionism with imperialism, but no economic transformation program is stated for the mainstream.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The Palestinian National Council acted as a constituent body in declaring statehood; inferred support for elected constitution-making.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The declaration promises freedoms; no growth rationale appears.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The movement depends on aid and endorses UN and Non-Aligned principles.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The declaration promises democratic government; the PA elected its president directly in 1996 and 2005, inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The PLO accepted 242 and 338 and negotiated for land and peace; the 1993 exchange of letters is premised on territorial compromise.

collective-defense.rationale: The Covenant urges Arab states to support Palestine, a collective-defense logic, but treaty alliances aren't discussed.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Palestinian nationalism rejects Israeli annexation of East Jerusalem and treats the 1967 territories as occupied.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Not addressed; the Covenant's indivisibility of Palestine suggests no stance on other states.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's own claim is sovereignty, with no stance on autonomy within a larger state.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The declaration sets a democratic constitutional order and the movement is republican and non-monarchical.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed by any source; irrelevant to the national liberation agenda.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The declaration promises a constitution and independent judiciary.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Not addressed by any source; the declaration chooses a parliamentary democracy without a mixed constitution.

leader-cult.rationale: Arafat's personality cult was real in the movement, yet formal doctrine is silent; split.

refugee-return.rationale: The return of 1948 refugees and descendants is the foremost Palestinian demand, grounded in UNGA 194 and 3236 and held non-negotiable by the PA.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The movement has no socialist programme in the secular PLO mainstream; inferred as rejection of a doctrine specific to Marxism-Leninism.

land-redistribution.rationale: The movement's founding documents do not address landed estates; the main land question is return of land lost to Israel, not redistribution between farmers and owners.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred: the claim to Palestine rests on the Palestinian Arab people's presence there, but the 1988-93 commitment is to the 1967 territories, not to areas beyond them.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The mainstream secular PLO and the 1988 Declaration guarantee freedom of belief and equality regardless of religion, though Islamist wings dissent.

women-must-cover.rationale: The 1988 Declaration commits to equality of rights regardless of sex and the secular mainstream does not seek dress laws; Hamas differs.

common-currency.rationale: Not addressed; Palestinian nationalists use shared currencies in practice but sovereignty over currency is a statehood demand, so no clear position.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The founding Covenant describes Palestinians as part of the Arab nation and Arab unity as a goal, though later practice prizes a separate Palestinian state.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The movement demands a sovereign state, not minority cultural autonomy within another state, and rejects that as an alternative.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The movement answers with a national homeland and return to Palestine, rejecting the idea that Palestinians should settle for equal rights elsewhere.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Inferred: a nationalist movement locates change in national will and politics, not modes of production, though some leftist factions differ.

ban-cartels.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; no economic doctrine can be sourced.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed; the movement has no worked-out position on financial rescue.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The 1988 Declaration promises a democratic state with rule of law and protected rights, which implies courts limit majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The Declaration promises equality of rights but sets no quota; inferred from PLO practice of women's representation.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inferred: the 1988 Declaration commits to peaceful coexistence and international cooperation, not closing off trade.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; no position can be inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; no position can be inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The 1968 Covenant holds that armed struggle by Palestinians themselves is the way to liberation, but the 1993 commitments renounced violence, and 'revolution' is not the frame.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is not anti-monarchical in principle and the Declaration is silent on titles.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred from the Covenant stress on Palestinian identity and heritage; the movement has no stated curriculum position.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The movement frames Zionism as colonial and itself as anti-colonial, so rule over a people for its supposed benefit is rejected.

patriotic-education.rationale: Inferred from the national-liberation framing of the Covenant and Declaration, which stress loyalty to the homeland; schooling is not addressed directly.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not a nationalist question; inferred from its colour-blind equality language, and consistent with its mild support for correcting injustice.

public-money-creation.rationale: The movement has no monetary program, so this is left neutral.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Not addressed; the movement has no shared view of capitalism and is split between secular and leftist factions.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Palestinian nationalism arose against British Mandate rule and rejects imperial claims, so it is inferred to reject cultivating influence in a predecessor empire's lands.

delink-world-market.rationale: The 1988 Declaration affirms non-alignment and economic cooperation, not delinking; there is no stated development doctrine.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Not addressed; only leftist factions such as the PFLP take a view and they are excluded from the scope.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The 1988 Declaration promises equality and no discrimination on grounds of race, religion or colour, which points against a right to discriminate.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Declaration commits to a democratic state guaranteeing rights and equality; entrenchment is inferred from that.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The Covenant and the 1988 declaration reject the Balfour Declaration and the Mandate as having no legal force, and treat the partition of Palestine as null.

elective-rulers.rationale: The 1988 declaration commits Palestine to a parliamentary democracy based on free elections and rejects hereditary rule.

minority-veto.rationale: The 1988 declaration describes majority rule with minority rights, not minority vetoes; inferred.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The movement has no stated doctrine about constitutional resistance to a ruler; its resistance doctrine concerns occupation.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The 1988 declaration envisages a parliamentary democracy; the point about monarchs is inferred from that.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: The movement does not address animals.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The movement does not address animal use.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: No documented position; the movement has no shared social programme.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Palestinian nationalism calls on every Palestinian to take part in the national struggle, and the Covenant makes it a duty.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not addressed by the mainstream movement.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Not addressed by the mainstream movement.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The 1988 declaration calls for a just international economic order, but the mainstream has no worked-out dependency theory; adherents are split between liberal and leftist views.

native-born-offices.rationale: The Covenant defines Palestinians by descent, but a rule reserving offices for the native-born is not documented.

party-own-road.rationale: Not addressed by the mainstream movement.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The Palestinian Authority and PLO have depended on foreign aid and sought development support, so reliance only on own resources is rejected by inference.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The 1988 declaration and the right-of-return claim demand restoration of Palestinian land and homes lost in 1948 and 1967, though the 1993 recognition limits the claim to the 1967 territories.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The Covenant makes the Palestinian Arabs the native people with sovereignty over Palestine, and treats Zionist settlers as lacking it, although the 1988 text offers equality to all citizens.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Not addressed; the movement has no common view on constitutional founding values of this kind.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Not addressed; the nationalist mainstream has no position on this comparison.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: No documented position; adherents would be expected to follow the mainstream account that slavery was the cause, which is inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The 1988 declaration adopts a democratic constitution on a general model while stressing Arab and national identity; no clear position on civilizational fit.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The PLO is itself an armed organisation, but a political guardian role for a state army is not a documented position.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from the strongly family-centred society the movement represents; the national texts do not address it.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred from the Declaration's commitment to parliamentary, elected government; exams for office are not addressed.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from the movement's stress on national control of the economy and resources; no stated policy on takeovers.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Adherents are split: the Declaration promises women equality, but personal-status law follows religious rules and the movement takes no position.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The Declaration commits to a parliamentary democracy with elected, regular-term government, not bound delegates; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the PLO-era state-provided social services and a mixed economy.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The Declaration sets out a modern state without collective land tenure; private ownership is assumed. Inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The Declaration commits to a parliamentary democracy, which implies legislative control of the budget; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: The Declaration pledges equality for all citizens regardless of religion, language or race and Arabic is the language of the nation, with no stated plan to restrict others; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The Covenant stresses defending Palestine's land and integrity from foreign takeover; inferred as a ban on land sales to outsiders.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from the movement's complaints of structural discrimination under occupation, which it judges by effect.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Not an issue the national texts address and adherents have no common view.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The Covenant endorses armed struggle and solidarity with liberation movements; inferred for foreign insurgencies.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The Covenant stresses Palestinian independent decision and the Arab nation's sovereignty; inferred that force against allies' choices is opposed.

corporate-influence.rationale: The movement has no shared position on lobbying or campaign finance; adherents' main concern is foreign influence over Palestine, not corporate power at home.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the sovereignty and self-determination framing of the Declaration of Independence; the PLO-era leadership has defended state control of its own institutions.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from the demographic framing of the conflict and the right-of-return claim, which stress growing the Palestinian population; no program states it.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from the movement's concern over land loss and dispossession, which favors protecting local land ownership; not a stated program item.

job-guarantee.rationale: Labor rights appear in the nationalist platform but no source states an employer-of-last-resort policy; adherents are not clearly for or against.

democratic-peace.rationale: The 1988 Declaration invokes democracy and peaceful coexistence, but adherents are generally skeptical that democratic states act peacefully toward Palestinians, so no clear stance.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Nationalism that builds a state on law and national legitimacy implies a duty to obey a legitimate national government; inferred, not stated.

non-intervention.rationale: Adherents reject outside interference in Palestinian affairs but also appeal to the UN and international bodies to act against occupation, so a flat ban on intervention is unlikely.

industrial-unions.rationale: Not addressed by the nationalist platform; trade-union federations exist in Palestine but no source ties the movement to a union structure.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The 1968 Covenant treats Zionism as a hostile movement, but the 1993 letters renounce this framing as a conspiracy against the nation; the mainstream rejects an ethnic-minority conspiracy claim.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the Covenant's emphasis on the family and on a descent-based national community; the movement has not sought to end legal marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The Declaration commits to a democratic state with rights and freedoms; open government follows from that, but it is not stated.

local-production.rationale: Not an issue the movement has addressed; no stated position on localism in production.

informal-organisation.rationale: The mainstream strand is organized through permanent bodies such as the PLO and Fatah, so it favors formal organization over small informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The movement relies on UN resolutions and international law in its claims (the 1988 Declaration, UN 242 and 338), so it does not put national law above international law.

religious-nation.rationale: The Declaration of Independence promises equality regardless of religion and the mainstream strand is secular; Islamist definitions of the nation are the dissenting Hamas strand.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The 1988 declaration commits to non-alignment and equality among states, so ritual submission to a leading power is inferred to be unwelcome.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The Covenant treats Palestine as an indivisible homeland, so keeping regional revenue apart from the whole is inferred to be disfavoured.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The mainstream movement has no property program; inferred as split between private ownership and leftist factions outside this scope.

defeat-communism.rationale: The mainstream took no crusading anti-communist line and was Soviet-aligned for decades, but is secular and non-communist; inferred as mild disagreement.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: No stated program on service delivery; adherents are split between state provision and private or NGO providers.

religion-illusion.rationale: The mainstream is secular but treats religion as part of Palestinian identity, so inferred to reject the claim that it will fade.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Not an issue the movement addressed; secular nationalists lack a settled view on capitalism as a historical stage.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The movement frames equality through law and the 1988 declaration pledge of equal rights, not economic transformation; inferred only.

socialized-care.rationale: No program for public housework services; family-centred social values are inferred to favour private care.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Arabic is central to identity but the movement has no purge policy; inferred from its general cultural nationalism.

treaties-binding.rationale: The 1993 letters rest on honouring agreements and UN resolutions, so lasting treaties are inferred to be valued by adherents.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The movement seeks a nation-state, not commune networks; inferred from the 1988 declaration state-building aims.

majority-settlement.rationale: Settlement of one group into another people's territory is the core grievance against Israel, so adherents would reject it as a policy; inferred from that.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: No stated position; the secular mainstream has no third-way doctrine and is split in practice.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The Covenant grounds the Palestinian claim on historical and Arab ties to the land and denies that Jewish historical ties give a title.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Fatah leaders have formally acknowledged the Holocaust, but adherents differ and some deny or minimise it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the Declaration promises equality without discrimination, while Palestinian society and law are largely conservative.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The 1988 Declaration promises a parliamentary democracy with pluralism, though the PA's actual record is more repressive.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The Declaration guarantees freedom of religion and equality, so the secular mainstream does not seek to punish blasphemy; Islamist strands differ.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The movement was born in opposition to mandate and colonial rule and to settler colonialism, and demands self-determination.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: The secular mainstream rests resistance on national and UN rights, not religious duty, while the Islamist wing holds the duty; the movement is split.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The secular PLO and Fatah mainstream rejects religious law as a test of legitimacy and set out a democratic, pluralist state.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Not addressed beyond general democratic commitments in the Declaration; adherents have no distinct view on direct participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The Declaration promises equality regardless of race, religion or sex, but the movement has no program on how oppressions interact.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from conservative social norms among most adherents.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the religious and social conservatism of Palestinian society.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The movement unites diverse factions around a national cause and has little economic left-right program, so it neither affirms nor denies the divide.

alienated-labor.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the mainstream has no worked-out economic theory, though leftist factions would agree.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The movement calls for a state that treats all faiths equally and sees conflict as national, not civilisational; Palestinians are themselves Muslims and Christians.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The 1988 Declaration bases the state on popular sovereignty and democracy, though it invokes religious heritage; the Islamist wing differs.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the Declaration's religious freedom suggests the mainstream would allow religious dress.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and the movement has no position on employment contracts.

social-market-economy.rationale: The movement has no shared economic program, and the Declaration says little beyond a free-market-leaning open economy and social justice.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The movement was founded on armed struggle for liberation and seeks a state that can defend itself, though the 1993 letters renounce terrorism.

rich-first.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the movement has no developmental doctrine and adherents are split.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The 1988 Declaration states a commitment to non-alignment and peaceful coexistence.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The 1988 Declaration commits to a democratic system and elected institutions; hereditary succession is inferred to be disfavoured, though Arab monarchies are allies.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The movement has no stated banking policy; inferred as indifferent.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Palestinian Authority finances depend on donors and lenders and no doctrine is stated; adherents are split.

property-franchise.rationale: The 1988 Declaration promises a democratic state with equal rights for all citizens, which excludes wealth qualifications for voting.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The Declaration promises equality of the sexes, but no link to the domination of nature is stated; inferred as split.

reification.rationale: This Marxist concept is not part of the nationalist program; inferred as indifferent.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The Declaration protects freedom of opinion and the press, but the movement has no doctrine on private media ownership; adherents split.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The 1988 Declaration promises a constitutional, democratic state under law; support is inferred from that, though the PLO itself ruled by decree.

racial-franchise.rationale: The 1988 Declaration states that equality and non-discrimination in rights apply regardless of race, religion or colour, which excludes restricting the vote to one ethnic group.

online-participation.rationale: The movement has no stated position; mild support is inferred from its democratic commitments and its reliance on diaspora participation.

open-government-data.rationale: Mild support is inferred from the democratic and rule-of-law commitments in the Declaration; the movement states no position.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Mainstream secular nationalism promises equality regardless of religion, but personal status law is religious in practice; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The 1988 Declaration rejects discrimination on religious grounds, and the PLO's secular nationalism does not target minority businesses.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The mainstream expects elected institutions and a parliamentary democracy, as the 1988 Declaration describes, and sortition is not part of the programme; inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The secular PLO/Fatah mainstream pledges equality and freedom of belief, so it leans toward modern reinterpretation over fixed classical rulings; inferred from the 1988 Declaration's tolerance language.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The movement has no shared economic programme; the sources do not address wealth concentration.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The mainstream secular strand has not endorsed it and the sources are silent; conservative social norms in the society are inferred.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The 1988 Declaration affirms religious tolerance and equality, and the movement is not committed to atheism; the state is expected to be neutral or respect faith.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The movement seeks a state with its own security forces and police; abolition is inferred as rejected.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The PLO set out a democratic state but has no stated view on formal power-sharing; adherents differ.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The movement has no stated position; refugee relief by agencies and community is a fact but no principle.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents have no common position.

vote-delegation.rationale: Not addressed; a delegation system is far from the party and assembly structures of the PLO, inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed; outside the movement's concerns.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Muslim and Christian adherents differ and the secular mainstream has no stated stance.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The 1988 Declaration promises equal rights regardless of sex, from which shared marital authority is inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The movement's concern is the status of Palestinians in their own homeland, not resident foreigners' voting; inferred as indifferent from the founding documents, which do not address it.

rent-control.rationale: Housing regulation is not part of the national program; the movement has little shared economic platform, so no direction can be inferred.

abolish-ip.rationale: Intellectual property is never addressed; the 1988 Declaration's commitment to a market-friendly, internationally integrated state suggests mild opposition to abolition, inferred.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Fatah ran youth movements (Ashbal, Zahrat) with paramilitary elements, but the secular mainstream has no doctrine of drilled national-service youth, so adherents are split.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed directly; the 1988 Declaration's commitment to peace and non-alignment suggests acceptance of a nuclear-free territory, inferred.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The 1988 Declaration commits to non-alignment and to a sovereign state free of foreign military control, and the nationalist case against occupation is a case against foreign troops on its soil.

recognise-genocide.rationale: The movement frames the 1948 expulsion (Nakba) as a mass dispossession it wants acknowledged, and demands recognition of past wrongs as part of the return claim.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The 1988 Declaration promises social justice and equality; the movement's mainstream is not a property-first ideology, but it has no worked-out doctrine on this, so inferred.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The PLO charter makes armed struggle a duty and legitimises force in defence of the homeland, so adherents reject absolute pacifism even when later renouncing terrorism.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The 1968 Covenant says Palestinians are an authentic nation with ties to the land stretching back through history, though the 1988 text frames it more modestly.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed; the movement has no position on gender theory, and adherents are split between conservative and secular strands.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed by the national movement; adherents are split and the sources are silent, so inferred as neutral.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Palestinian nationalism holds fighters and civilians killed in the struggle to be shuhada (martyrs), a central honour in Fatah and PLO culture; martyrs' families receive state support.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The secular PLO/Fatah mainstream frames its struggle as national and political, not as a cosmic spiritual contest; that framing belongs to the Islamist wing excluded from this scope.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The Covenant and the right of return place the homeland at the centre of Palestinian identity, but the mainstream wants the refugees to return, not merely to look to a homeland as a cultural centre, so mild agreement at most.

culture-before-state.rationale: The movement put state-building and liberation first, declaring independence in 1988 before cultural renewal, and the mainstream treats statehood as the precondition of national life.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; the secular mainstream is silent on theology and adherents span Muslim and Christian communities.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed by the national movement; adherents are split between religious conservatives and secular feminists.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The 1988 Declaration promises equality regardless of religion or race, and the Palestinian state is meant to be democratic and pluralist, which is at odds with rule by a national majority alone.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The movement claims Palestine as indivisible, as a single unit for the whole people, and does not endorse carving up regions by people; inferred from the Covenant's indivisibility claim.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist platform's labour-rights emphasis; Palestinian unions have mostly been tied to factions, so the stance is mild.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Mainstream Fatah/PLO nationalism has no stated socialist programme; the claim belongs to leftist factions excluded from this scope.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from PLO-era social services and the 1988 declaration's commitment to social justice, though there is no worked-out policy.

second-chamber.rationale: Not addressed; the Palestinian Authority has a single legislative council and the movement has no doctrine on bicameralism.

municipal-property.rationale: The mainstream has no collectivist programme and its 1988 declaration protects private property and a pluralist economy, so community ownership is not supported.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Not addressed; the movement stresses a unified national leadership and state, though local councils have a role under the Authority.

family-wage.rationale: Not addressed; no position can be drawn from the sources.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: The question lies outside the movement's concerns; no position can be inferred.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: The question lies outside the movement's concerns; no position can be inferred.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not addressed; the Palestinian economy depends on a financial system controlled by Israel, which makes untraceable payments appealing, but the movement takes no stated view.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; no stated position, and the Authority has restricted online speech while activists favour anonymity, so adherents are split.

person-over-state.rationale: The 1988 declaration affirms individual rights and equality for all citizens, which fits the idea; the Kantian wording is not used, so the answer is inferred.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The secular PLO/Fatah mainstream honours Islam and Christianity in its declaration but does not hold politics should serve a spiritual nature; the Islamist wing is excluded from this scope.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Not addressed; the nationalist aim is a single sovereign state, and the movement has no stated view on regional autonomy.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic and unrelated to the movement; no position can be inferred.

dense-cities.rationale: Unrelated to the movement; no position can be inferred.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Palestinian nationalism defines a national, not racial, group and the 1988 declaration rejects discrimination on grounds of race, so organising by race is disfavoured.

racial-pride.rationale: The movement stresses national and cultural pride, not racial pride, so the literal statement is not clearly addressed.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Mainstream nationalism renounced terrorism in 1993 but kept the right to resist occupation, and the 1968 covenant endorsed armed struggle, so the answer is split.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Palestinians see themselves as part of the Arab nation, and the Covenant ties them to Arab unity, but it defines Palestinian identity by descent and homeland rather than language, so this is inferred.

communal-electorates.rationale: The 1988 Declaration promises equality regardless of religion and a democratic parliamentary system, which points to common electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The movement reads Zionism and outside powers as having divided and dispossessed Palestine; the claim about a continuing plot is inferred from that framing.

free-public-college.rationale: No stated program on tuition; inferred from the nationalist emphasis on education and social rights in the Declaration.

pollution-taxes.rationale: The movement has no environmental tax program and adherents have no settled view; left neutral.

future-generations.rationale: Not a stated issue; inferred from the strong stress on land and heritage handed down to later generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The Declaration stresses equality of rights between women and men, not distinct values; inferred that adherents would not assign women a separate weight.

arms-reduction.rationale: Adherents combine a wish for a demilitarised peace with insistence on security and resistance to occupation; the sources do not settle it.

open-diplomacy.rationale: The Declaration and the 1993 letters appeal to UN legitimacy and public commitments; open diplomacy is inferred from that, not stated.

capital-controls.rationale: The movement has no worked-out economic program and the Palestinian economy is tied to Israel's currency and trade; adherents are not settled.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The PLO accepted a single authority in principle and the Palestinian Authority claims a security monopoly, but factions have kept arms and the movement upholds armed resistance; contested among adherents.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The movement upholds armed struggle against occupation as legitimate, so refusing to fight would not be its view; inferred from the Covenant and PLO practice.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The movement has no worked-out labour program; Palestinian unions were part of PLO institutions but bargaining is not a defining issue.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: The movement has no position on wage supplements and adherents span left to conservative.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The movement has no stated position on fiscal rules, and its economy depends on aid and Israeli-controlled revenues.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Palestinian nationalists frame their cause with the anti-colonial and third-world movements and support a fairer international order; inferred, not stated in the sources.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The movement seeks to build its own state institutions, not smash them, and the PA took over administration under the Oslo framework; inferred.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The movement has no economic blueprint, so it is neither for nor against pluralism of systems.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Ecological valuation is not part of the movement's program.

sacred-nation.rationale: Palestinian nationalism treats the homeland and Al-Quds as holy and the nation as enduring through exile, though the secular mainstream states this in national rather than religious terms; inferred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: The movement has no position on student loans and adherents are not aligned.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The movement's colonialism claim concerns Israel and the occupation, not regional exploitation inside one state, so the statement is largely off-topic.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The movement does not address human nature; the 1988 declaration invokes universal rights but without a view on a fixed nature.

public-service-media.rationale: The movement has no position on public service media; PLO-era broadcasting was a party and state organ, and adherents are not aligned.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The Declaration respects all faiths in Palestine, but the secular movement took no position on whether religions share one truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Farm policy is not part of the nationalist programme, which has little shared economic platform.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The movement is a stateless one with no nuclear programme and has no stated position on others' arsenals.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred from Fatah and the PLO being a broad national front that unites all classes under one liberation movement, rather than a class party.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the 1988 Declaration's commitment to equality and democracy and its rejection of discrimination; FGM is not discussed.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The 1988 Declaration promises equal rights regardless of religion, race or sex, which supports equal legal rights for women.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Inferred from the Covenant's definition of Palestinians as part of the Arab nation sharing Arabic language and culture; the question of regional naming is not addressed.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Pollution liability is outside the national movement's concerns and no position follows from its principles.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from the Declaration's commitment to a democratic parliamentary state, which leaves no formal legislative role for chiefs; not discussed directly.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Environment-versus-liberty trade-offs are not part of the national programme.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Sentencing policy is not part of the national programme and nothing in the sources bears on it.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The sources say nothing about immigration or language requirements, and the movement's concern is return of refugees, not immigration.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The movement has no worked-out labour policy; Fatah-aligned unions were state-linked, but no settled view on dues exists.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed by the nationalist documents; adherents have no settled view and the question is tied to local election law.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The 1988 declaration safeguards religious convictions and cites a heritage of tolerance and religious coexistence, which implies equal treatment of faiths, though it names no rule on interpretations within one religion.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The 1988 declaration pairs a parliamentary democratic system with social justice and equality of rights, so adherents want both elections and substance.

premarital-sex.rationale: Mainstream secular nationalists are mixed and the movement has no program on sexual morality; Islamist and conservative strands disagree.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred: the movement faces Israeli control of its communications and the declaration promises freedom of expression, so it leans against shutdowns.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: no stated welfare policy; the declaration's social justice language favours kept programmes over replacing them with a single payment.

women-suffrage.rationale: The 1988 declaration promises equality and non-discrimination in public rights on grounds of race, religion, color or sex under a parliamentary democratic system.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Mainstream secular nationalism has not blamed religion for women's status, and the Islamist wing would reject the claim; inferred split.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred: the declaration bars discrimination on race and the movement draws national identity from history and culture, not descent.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred: the PLO built a women's union and the declaration promises non-discrimination on sex, so state bodies for equality fit.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Nationalists treat Palestine's land as the collective patrimony of the Palestinian people; first-claim private ownership is inferred as disfavoured from that framing.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: The 1988 declaration grounds statehood in UN legitimacy and international law, which implies support for international accountability mechanisms.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The mainstream PLO/Fatah strand is secular and does not take scripture as inerrant law; inferred from that secular character, with Islamist strands dissenting.

gendered-self-government.rationale: The 1988 declaration pledges equal rights for all citizens regardless of religion, race or sex.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The movement was non-aligned and has no planned-economy doctrine; inferred from its non-alignment and lack of a shared economic programme.

indirect-election.rationale: Palestinian institutions and the 1988 declaration stress democratic, pluralist parliamentary rule; indirect selection is inferred as disfavoured, not stated.

national-church-status.rationale: The 1988 declaration promises equality of all religions before the law, against a privileged religious body.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Self-rule for Palestinians as a national group, within the state or as autonomy, is the core demand; extended by inference to regional autonomy for minorities.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Palestinian nationalists hold that the whole Palestinian people, refugees included, decide the territory's fate, not only current local inhabitants; inferred, not stated.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: The 1968 Covenant defines Palestine within its British Mandate boundaries as an indivisible unit, so inherited colonial-era borders are the claimed frame (the 1988-93 position narrows this to the 1967 lines).

simple-living.rationale: The movement has no teaching on austerity or self-sufficiency; inferred as not endorsing it from its development-oriented statehood goals.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Opposition to settlement of outsiders on Palestinian land is central, and the Covenant limits those treated as Palestinian to those resident before the Zionist invasion.

equal-conscription.rationale: The Covenant calls on all Palestinians to join the struggle; inferred that any draft would bind women and men alike.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The Covenant calls Palestine the homeland of the Arab Palestinian people and the liberation of it a national duty.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream PLO/Fatah commits to rule of law and, after 1993, to renouncing terrorism; the movement addresses no such policy.

close-ties-china.rationale: Inferred from the PLO's non-aligned, Third World diplomacy, not from a stated position on China.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred: the PLO claims to represent Palestinians everywhere including the diaspora and refugees, though this is not about minorities in neighbouring states as such.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The movement has no shared economic programme, so this is not a stated position.

self-ownership.rationale: No shared position; the movement is defined by national questions and not by property theory.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: No shared economic programme on taxation exists in the sources.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: No shared welfare programme; the movement is defined by national questions.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred: the PLO is itself a coalition of factions and parties, so adherents defend organised politics over rule by a single leader.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from the 1988 declaration's commitment to equality and democratic pluralism, not from any statement on business.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The 1988 declaration guarantees equality regardless of religion and the mainstream PLO is secular, though Hamas dissents.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: No shared position; adherents range from secular modernisers to traditionalists.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from the 1988 declaration's pledge of equal rights for women and men.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred: sovereignty over Palestinian land is central, but the sources state no resource policy.

missingStatements.text: Refugees who fled or were expelled from a conflict should be allowed to return to the homes they left, and their descendants too.
missingStatements.rationale: The return of 1948 refugees and descendants is the foremost Palestinian demand, grounded in UNGA 194 and 3236 and held non-negotiable by the PA.

missingStatements.text: East Jerusalem should be the capital of a Palestinian state.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1988 declaration names Jerusalem (Al-Quds) as capital of Palestine, and East Jerusalem is a core claim in later negotiations.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to one conflict; the capital question is covered by jewish-state-israel and annexed-territory-occupation.

missingStatements.text: Populations settled by an occupying power in occupied territory should be removed.
missingStatements.rationale: Settlement is described as a primary obstacle in the peace process and Palestinian nationalism rejects occupation of the 1967 territories.
missingStatements.declined: Covered loosely by annexed-territory-occupation and settler-state-colonial; too conflict-specific for a new statement.

notes: Hamas and other Islamist nationalists answer differently on laws from scripture, clerical influence, armed struggle, recognition of Israel and borders (all of Mandatory Palestine). The 1968 Covenant took positions on Israel's legitimacy and armed struggle that the PLO later declared inoperative in 1993; this profile follows the later commitments. Most economic and social statements are unaddressed by the movement and are low confidence.
